The Selvage of GJ 1002 b

A real planet, 15.8 light-years away, with an imagined shore. GJ 1002 b keeps one face to a red dwarf. Between day and night runs the Selvage, the ring where a wide ember of a sun bobs above and below the horizon once every 10.35 days, and brine flats flood and dry on that beat.

The crust is thin sheets of mineral, stacked A, B or C. Nothing here has a body. Look at the ground where things are, and it is a restless flicker with no edges. Look at it by when, and several things turn out to be in the same place. This is the story Phase Slip, put to the test: no tempo is programmed in. The first draft failed parts of the test, and the story was revised to match.
